District & Sessions Judge-FTSC-1,
Hassan, arising out of Crime No.27/2024 registered by Hassan Women Police Station, Hassan District for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 & 506 of IPC & Sections 6, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is before this Court seeking regular bail.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.27/2024 was registered by Hassan Women Police Station, Hassan District initially against unknown person for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC, on the basis of first information dated 17.04.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein who is the father of the victim girl, aged 17 years as on the date of first information.

entities.text: Hassan Women Police Station, Hassan District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced.
The petitioner was arrested and produced before the jurisdictional Court NC: 2024:KHC:37756 on 26.04.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
4. The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Sessions Court in Spl.C.No.306/2024 was dismissed on 29.07.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner and the victim girl are in love and the victim girl had voluntarily accompanied the petitioner and traveled together with him to Delhi.
Thereafter, they had returned to Bengaluru.
They had stayed for a period of ten days in Delhi.
The victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, about he committing sexual assault on her against her wishes.
He refers to medical examination report of the victim girl and submits that the word 'Sexual intercourse' has been inserted subsequently in the report.

He submits that the petitioner has no NC:
2024:KHC:37756 criminal antecedents.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 have opposed the petition.
They submit that the victim girl was a minor as on the date of first information and therefore the alleged offences get attracted against the petitioner.
They submit that in the event the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he is likely to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
They also submit that in the charge sheet it is alleged that the petitioner had sexually assaulted the victim girl.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.
7. The material on record would go to show that after the victim girl was found missing from her house on 16.04.2024 efforts were made to trace her.

Since the victim girl was not traced, on 17.04.2024, the first informant had approached the police and submitted his first information,
based on which FIR in Crime No.27/2024 NC: 2024:KHC:37756 was initially registered against unknown person for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced.
The statement of the victim girl was recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 13.05.2024 and as on the said date, the victim girl had already completed her 18 years of age.

8. A perusal of the statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, would go to show that she and the petitioner were acquainted to each other and she had voluntarily gone along with him in a car to Bengaluru and thereafter they had traveled together to Delhi in a aeroplane and stayed together in ahouse for a period of nearly 10 days.
She has not made any allegation against the petitioner that he had sexually assaulted her while staying with him at Delhi, except stating that he had physically touched her.
In her statement made before the doctor who had medically examined her she has stated that she is in love with the petitioner for the last four NC: 2024:KHC:37756 years.
Since her parents refused for their marriage they had left the house and had gone to Delhi and stayed together.
She has stated that they both kissed and hugged each other during their stay in Delhi for ten days.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has pointed out that the word 'sexual intercourse' has been inserted subsequently in the medical documents.

9. Be that as it may, the fact remains that in the statement recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C, the victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner of he having sexual intercourse with her.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Undisputedly, the petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Apprehension of the learned counsel for respondents can be taken care of by imposing appropriate conditions.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
